    {"name": "direction_filmmaking_assessment", "analytical_usefulness": 0.85, "source_groundedness": 0.65, "rationale": "Useful aspect but groundedness is weaker.     {"name": "plot_narrative_structure_focus", "analytical_usefulness": 0.9, "source_groundedness": 0.75, "rationale": "Genuine axis for grouping.     {"name": "genre_tone_execution", "analytical_usefulness": 0.8, "source_groundedness": 0.6, "rationale": "Relevant dimension, but the value 'mismatched_to_genre_expectations' appears heavily and is often not clearly supported by the source (a bad movie is not the same as genre-mismatched).     {"name": "entertainment_engagement_verdict", "analytical_usefulness": 0.75, "source_groundedness": 0.8, "rationale": "Useful overall engagement axis, somewhat overlaps with sentiment but adds a boring/watchable gradient. Samples reasonably grounded (insipid/boring -> boring_or_slow, 'pile of crap' -> unwatchable)."},
    {"name": "comparison_or_adaptation_reference", "analytical_usefulness": 0.85, "source_groundedness": 0.7, "rationale": "Distinct categorical axis about what reviewers reference. Mostly grounded (Stargate compared to Star Trek -> compared_to_other_films; Stephen King name -> reasonable), though IMDB-0002 labeled 'director_or_actor_body_of_work' from a writing-credit mention is a mild stretch."}
  ],
  "analytical_usefulness": 0.85,
  "source_groundedness": 0.74,
  "rationale": "The added columns decompose reviewer focus into meaningful, distinct aspects (acting, script, direction, plot, genre/tone, engagement, comparisons), each offering a genuine grouping/comparison axis directly serving the query about what reviewers focus on. Groundedness is generally good, with appropriate not_present handling for silent rows. The main weaknesses are over-attribution in direction_filmmaking and genre_tone_execution, where confident negative/mismatch labels are asserted without clear textual support, indicating some hallucination on those axes."
